characters.description: The central protagonist. A young up and coming racing driver filled with determination who drives the Mach 5. The Ace: Speed has proven time and time again to be one of the best racers in the entire business, taking on some of the most dangerous racers and tracks in sports. When pushed to fight, he's also an extremely accurate shot with a firearm and has won quite his fair share of brawls when he has a chance. In the end, Speed almost always comes on top. Adaptational Jerkass: In the original manga, Mifune was a genuinely kind-hearted individual that only fought if he absolutely had to, to the point that one villain expresses aVillain Respectfor him as one of the greatest men in the world by heart and honor alone. In the anime by comparison, he's far more willing to jump to gunning down and killing those that threaten the people around him or his own life, which clashes significantly withIncorruptible Pure Purenesshe originated as. Badass Driver: He's no slouch when it comes to being a racing driver. Berserk Button: Do notevercall Speed a coward or doubt his ability to race. Sometimes he has a light-hearted tantrum. Other times he's flipped out and made reckless to near-suicidal decisions that can endanger those around him. One time he grabbed Sparky by the collar of his shirt and seemed like he was about to throttle the kid due to the latter's concern over the cheating bad guys he'd have to race against.

characters.name: Spritle Racer (Kurio Mifune) and Chim Chim (Sanpei)
characters.description: Spritle is Speed's younger brother. Always following along on adventures by sneaking into the trunk of the Mach 5. Chim Chim is his pet monkey Amplified Animal Aptitude: Chim Chim. Annoying Younger Sibling: Downplayed, as Speed doesn't usually mind Spritle. That said, he can get fed up with his whining (see The Most Dangerous Race episodes). Bratty Half-Pint: Spritle tends to be like this towards the older characters. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: The two of them might seem like a hapless child and a silly chimpanzee, but the two of them have proven to be able to hold their own against actual threats.

characters.name: Pops Racer (Daisuke Mifune)
characters.description: A talented engineer who built the Mach 5. Is the father of Rex, Speed and Spritle. Action Dad: Much like his children, he's very capable of kicking ass.As champion of the Westside Grunters and Groaners I promise you are in for a lot of groaning! Badass Driver: Like father, like son. The Engineer: Pops is a brilliant engineer, having created the Mach 5, which is largely considered to be one of the most advanced racing vehicles in the world. Fantasy-Forbidding Father: He was one towards Rex, but he grows out of it by the time Speed is a young adult.

characters.name: Mom Racer (Aya Mifune)
characters.description: The mother of Rex, Speed and Spritle. Good Parents: Towards Speed, Spritle and Rex. Happily Married: To her beloved husband, Pops. Nice Girl: She's a kind woman, never shown to have a negative attitude towards anyone throughout the series. Only Sane Woman: Relatively; she's the only person within the series (outside of perhaps Inspector Detector) to never have an extreme moment of emotion.

characters.name: Rex Racer (Ken'ichi Mifune), aka Racer X (The Masked Racer)
characters.description: Speed's older brother who ran away from home years ago to become a racing driver. He keeps his identity hidden by entering competitions as Racer X. Also works for Interpol as Agent 9. Drives the Shooting Star. Badass Driver: It should be expected given that he's Speed Racer's brother. Big Brother Instinct: Very protective of Speed and Spritle. Big Brother Mentor: Will provide Speed with advice and guidance when ever he can. This is especially ironic since Racer X actuallyishis older brother, making this a literal example of the trope, but Speed is completely unaware of it. Black Knight: He is a feared and brooding international spy often seen thwarting evil schemes.

characters.name: Trixie (Michi Shimura)
characters.description: Speed's forceful girlfriend. During races she often follows him from above in her helicopter, acting as a spotter. Action Girlfriend: Manages to throw a few punches against Speed's foes when she is a passenger in the Mach 5 during races. Clingy Jealous Girl: She gets jealous if Speed is with another girl that is at her age, even if Speed is just being friendly towards the other. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Despite her tendency to be aClingy Jealous Girlto any girl that gets close to Speed, she is otherwise a loving girlfriend to him. Mission Control: During races, she is most often seen in her helicopter above the Mach 5, radio-relaying information to Speed.

characters.name: Sparky (Sabu)
characters.description: A mechanic who works for Pops and is the best friend of Speed. Grease Monkey: Works as a mechanic and knows more about the inner workings of the Mach 5 than anyone else, except for Pops. Green-Eyed Monster: Sparky gets jealous that he doesn't get to be with Speed during some of the big races and instead Trixie joins. He does get his turn in the final episode. Nice Guy: One of the kindest characters in the show. Almost never gets angry.

characters.name: Inspector Detector (Detective Rokugo)
characters.description: A police officer with Interpol who investigates criminal activity. Quickly becomes an ally of Speed. Friend on the Force: A good friend of Speed's and distinguished police officer. Interpol Special Agent: As a member of the International Police, the inspector moves around the world. Reasonable Authority Figure: Always listens Speed when he stumbles upon a criminal plot. Steven Ulysses Perhero: He's an Inspector who's name is Inspector Detector.

characters.name: Car Acrobatic Team
characters.description: A group of rival racers, with a reputation for doing whatever it takes to win a race. Enemy Mine: They form one with Speed in "The Trick Race." Jerk Jock: Most of them are talented racers, and they will frequently show off their skills by performing tricks. Never My Fault: All of them blame Speed for Snake's injury. Never mind the fact Speed tried to warn Snake about his car leaking gas, but Snake wouldn't listen. That said, however, it’s possible that Snake didn’t tell the others that he had ignored Speed’s warning. The Rival: They're the closest thing Speed has to one outside ofRacer X,but we only see them for two arcs out of the entire show.

characters.name: Flash Marker Jr.
characters.description: Antagonist of "Race for Revenge." He uses his deceased father's car to get revenge on the ones who killed him. Big Brother Bully: Towards Lily. Death by Adaptation: Flash survived the helicopter crash in the manga, and was convinced by Speed toturn over a new leaf. His anime counterpart, unfortunately, wasn't very lucky. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: His motive for his actions against the Three Roses Club was revenge for killing his father and despite him being aBig Brother Bullytowards Lily, he still loves her. Used to Be a Sweet Kid: Near the end of the episode Lily implies that he was once a good kid before the Three Roses Club killed their father.

characters.name: Gadge Zoomer
characters.description: A former racing driver who becomes the champion car wrestler in "The Great Car Wrestling Match." Vehicular Combat: Makes his living competing by competing in "Car Wrestling" which is essentially a more violent version of demolition derby.

characters.name: Dr.McFife
characters.description: A mad scientist who built the terrifying monster car to gain revenge in "Car with a Brain." Mad Scientist: Used to be a brilliant scientist, but went insane and constructed the "Monster Car," a huge automobile controlled by a computer, which then went on a rampage.

characters.name: Karat Goldminter
characters.description: "The richest man in the world." Hosts the Around the World Grand Prix, in the episode "Race Around the World," offering a "small mountain of the purest gold" and his daughter's hand in marriage to the winner. Engagement Challenge: An incredibly wealthy man who holds the great Around the World Grand Prix and offers his daughter's hand in marriage to the person who wins it.

characters.name: Lovelace Goldminter
characters.description: Daughter of Karat Goldminter. Engagement Challenge: Daughter of Karat Goldminter. Enters the Around the World Grand Prix hoping to disrupt it and thus not be forced to marry the winner.

characters.name: Cruncher Block
characters.description: A gangster known for brutality and dirty dealings, whom Royalton uses as a leg-breaker. Big Badass Rig: He and his gang drive the Mammoth Car big rig, complete with gun ports and a front-mounted missile launcher. Dark Is Evil: He's a gangster who wears black and red clothes, and isThe Heavyof the film. Evil Brit: Cruncher has the Cockney accent befitting of aLondon Gangstercourtesy of the late John Benfield. The Heavy: When Royalton needs blackmailing, threatening or dirty deeds done, Cruncher and his gang take care of the back-alley heavy lifting, and other than the racers, they are the ones seen in active combat with the heroes.

characters.name: Mark Meglaton
characters.description: Burn Baby Burn: In hisVillainous Breakdown, he attempts to incinerate the works of art he had Speed steal when he fails to get his hands on the rocket fuel that he was trying to steal. Laughing Mad: He starts laughing histerically after attempting to set the works of art on fire. Malevolent Masked Man: Wears a mask for most of the episode and is an art thief. Villainous Breakdown: He goes down screaming at Speed and The Scientist he kidnapped to let the works of art he nicked burn. Villain of the Week: Only appears in "The Man Behind The Mask" where he was the titular antagonist.]

characters.name: Speed Racer
characters.description: The Ace: Dashingly handsome, Check. Talented driver, Check. Beautiful girlfriend, Check. Loving family, Check. Instincts to fully defy the laws of physics, Double Check. Adaptational Dumbass: Speed is shown to have beenBook Dumbthroughout school. This is in contrast to his anime counterpart, who was shown to be very adept and intelligent, with him and Trixie solving an Egyptian mystery through historical research. Adaptational Nice Guy: He's much more pleasant and nice (closer to his personality in the manga) than in the original anime. Badass Driver: It should go without saying. Battle Couple: With Trixie.

characters.name: Mom Racer
characters.description: Ascended Extra: While in the original series, she is a minor character with limited dialogue, in the movie, Susan Sarandon plays her as a strong, caring mother who provides emotional support and inspiration for Speed. Good Parents: One of the most supportive and caring people on Speed's side. The Heart: Mom's primary role in the family. She supplies food for everyone when the Racers are constructing the Mach 6, and is the one who breaks up a nasty argument between Speed and Pops and convinces the family to stay after Speed goes to Casa Cristo.

characters.name: Spritle and Chim Chim
characters.description: Annoying Younger Sibling: Speed really wishes Spritle and Chim Chim would stop sneaking into the trunk of his car. Big Brother Worship: He idealizes Speed the same way Speed used to idealize Rex. Brats with Slingshots: Uses a slingshot to distract Cruncher Block, giving the heroes a chance to rally. Dung Fu: In the middle of Cruncher and goons holding the heroes at gun point, Chim Chim throws his "Monkey Cookies" at him, instigating the fight. Kid Hero: Both of them put in quite a bit of work fighting people throughout, most notably Cruncher's goons. They were also the first to spot Royalton installing illegal spear hooks into their racecars.

characters.name: Pops Racer
characters.description: Destination Defenestration: Pops dumps the ninja who infiltrated the Racers' hotel room onto their wheeled dinner table and then kicks him out of their window. Good Parents: To Speed, Spritle and his long-lost child Rex. He misses Rex so much that he fears Speed might up and run away like him, but also reminds him that if he does he will always wait for him to come home. Happily Married: Mom and Pops Racer. Pops goes so far as to say marrying his best friend was the most important thing he'd ever done in his life, above and beyond his sons. Papa Wolf: Harm one of Pops's sons, and you will be sent flying through a window. Just ask thenon-ja. Parents as People: Pops let his pride get the better of him, disowning Rex when he defected Racer Motors to race for another company."I didn't lose Rex when he crashed. I lost him here. I let him think that a stupid motor company meant more to me than he did."

characters.name: Rex Racer
characters.description: Adaptational Angst Upgrade:In the original anime, Rex Racer merely ran away from home and disappeared before assuming the disguise of Racer X. In the film, Rex faked his own death to protect his family from the shady figures he had become embroiled with, leaving both of him and Pops with even guiltier consciences overtheir last interaction. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the original anime, Rex Racer ran away from home after getting into an argument with Pops over wrecking the Mach 1 during his first professional race. In the film, Rex was already a racing legend who had a falling out with Pops after Rex got involved with several scandals over alleged cheating on the race track.While in the anime, Rex became Racer X to prove to Pops that he could strike out on his own as a capable racer, in the film, he assumed a new identity in order to protect his family from the enemies he had made combating the corporations involved in race fixing. Big Brother Mentor: Rex was the one who taught Speed how to become a great race car driver. Death by Adaptation: In the anime, Rex merely ran away from home and never came back. In the movie, he ran away from home then died in a driving accident.Except he was actuallyFaking the Deadin order to protect his family. Magic Plastic Surgery:The film uses it as an explanation of how Rex went from looking like Scott Porter to Matthew Fox, showing that Rex completely changed his face to keep his family safe.

characters.name: Trixie
characters.description: Action Girl: Trixie was fairly tough in the anime, a novel concept at the time, but in the movie is much more an active partner to Speed than in the original.Even taking part in a portion of one of the races. Adaptational Badass: As opposed to the original anime, Trixie is aBadass Driverwho cancover for Taejo in the Casa Cristo. Badass Driver: This version of Trixie can drive just as well as Speed. She even gotPromoted to Playablein the film's video game tie-in, receiving her own T-180 racer in the process. The Big Damn Kiss: With Speed, at the end of the Grand Prix. Battle Couple: With Speed.

characters.name: Sparky
characters.description: Age Lift: Sparky and Speed were close in age in the original series, whereas here Sparky is older and closer to Rex in age. Awesome Aussie: Melbourne-born Kick Gurry uses his native accent as Sparky. Butt-Monkey: No matter the opponent, Sparky always ends up on his ass in a fight. Even gettingKOedby Cruncher Block, without even looking. Muscles Are Meaningless: Sparky may be a bit more lean than Speed, but he still looks at least as well-built as him (being a mechanic isn't exactly light work), yet he always gets his ass handed to him during the fight scenes. Non-Action Guy: In comparison to the rest of the Racer family. Even Spritle and Chim-Chim put up more of a fight against Cruncher Block's goons than he does.

characters.name: Arnold Royalton
characters.description: Big Bad: Of the movie. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Acts all friendly to the Racer family, only to reveal he's a nasty piece of work when Speed declines his offer. Break the Haughty: His smug demeanor shatters when he realizes his attempts to cheat in the Grand Prix are exposed and his reputation is irreparably ruined. He can only scream in rage as he loses everything. Break Them by Talking: He hurts Speed's morale with aMotive Rantthat demonstrates the long history of race fixing by corporate bigshots like himself. Connections Are Not Power: No matter how much authority he has when it comes to the World Racing League, it ends up proving fruitless after his corruption was exposed and he gets hauled off to jail.

characters.name: Jack "Cannonball" Taylor
characters.description: A racing driver for Royalton Industries. He is one of the best drivers in the World Racing League, but is known to play dirty. Cheaters Never Prosper: His attempt at taking Speed out with an illegal Spearhook during the final race costs him the Hall of Fame. Hoist by His Own Petard: His attempt to win the race by cheating with a Spearhook ends up backfiring when Speed exposes the use of the illegal device on camera. Humiliation Conga: Suffice to say his one-on-one duel with Speed at the Grand Prix ended up going really bad for Cannonball. Role-Ending Misdemeanor: In-Universe. After his use of a spear hook illegally gets exposed, his racing career is certainly going to be over.

characters.name: Snake Oiler
characters.description: A rival racer to Speed, in cahoots with the criminal Cruncher Block. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: After he tries to knock Taejo (really a disguised Trixie) off the road, an incensed Speed knocks him off and turns the tables on him, threatening to put the Mach 5's tyres right through his windshield while Snake pleads for his life. Animal Motifs: Look at his name, his scale-patterned racing gear and his snake-styled car and take a guess. Boisterous Weakling: The reason Cruncher Block hires additional mercenaries to take part in the Casa Cristo 5000 and knock off the Togokahn team is because Snake isn't competent enough to do the job, despite his whining. Cheaters Never Prosper: His cars are just as full of weapons as any other in the Casa Cristo, from snake-launchers to oil slicks, but they don't help him beat Speed. He even resorts to using ahandgun.

characters.name: Racer X
characters.description: The "Harbinger of Boom" and Speed's main rival on the race track. Adaptational Dye-Job: Goes from wearing a white suit and black mask to a black uniform with white X's. The Dreaded: He's feared both on and off the race track, to the point where Cruncher Block and his goons shit their pants when they realize Racer X is pursuing them. Friendly Rival: He's this to Speed, being affable with him off the track and even sometimes going out of his way to save Speed's lifeonthe track.Of course, it's hisBig Brother Instinctkicking in. Red Baron: "The Harbinger of Boom".

characters.name: Taejo Togokahn
characters.description: A talented racing driver and heir to Togokhan Motors. Affably Evil:While calling him "evil" might be pushing it a bit, Taejo is extremely polite and friendly towards Speed, even cheering for him as Speed wins the Grand Prix. He also looks impressed when he finds out that his sister went behind his back to get Speed the invite to the Grand Prix and never bothers to expose her. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Cruncher Block threatens to havehis hands eaten by piranhas.Taejo: No, please! Changed My Mind, Kid: One post-finale.Taejo initially left Inspector Detector and the Racers high and dry by using them to win Casa Cristo, drive up the price of his father's company for a bigger buyout, and leave without giving them any evidence of Royalton's connection to Cruncher Block, but inspired by Speed's Grand Prix victory, he decides to testify in court and put Royalton behind bars for good. Heel–Face Revolving Door: He asks Speed for help winning the Crucible to avoid Royalton buying his company from him, and they race in The Crucible together as teammates.Later it is revealed that he only intended to win the Crucible to increase the price of his company's stock, so he could sell out to Royalton for more money. Taejo, however, does not harbor any ill will towards Speed or his sister and even cheers for Speed during the Grand Prix at the end of the movie. At some point after the Grand Prix, Taejo broke off Togokhan Motors' partnership with Royalton and testified against Royalton and Block, leading to their convictions for fixing the WRL.

characters.name: Horuko Togokahn
characters.description: Action Girl: In the midst of the big battle against Crusher Rex and his goons, she's shown to be just as capable a fighter as everyone else. Loophole Abuse:After her father and brother Taejo use Speed Racer, Racer X and Inspector Detector to win the Casa Cristo 5000 and leave without giving them what they wanted (evidence against Cruncher Block and Royalton), an incensed Horuko gives Speed a invitation to the Grand Prix, which (according to the rules), Speed may participate in by virtue of being part of the "winning team" at Casa Cristo. Ms. Fanservice: A very lovely young lady, who (up until she destroys her family's evil plotting), serves next to no purpose in the film other than looking hot. Nice Girl:Unlike the rest of her family,Horuko's a sweetheart, and totally honest. Pretty in Mink: Horuko shows up to help the Speed family, coming straight from the opera, and wearing a white dress with a white fox fur wrap.

characters.name: Ben Burns
characters.description: A race commentator and former racing champion. Alliterative Name:BenBurns Broken Pedestal: Poor Speed, in regards to his racing hero, when he learns that the Grand Prix is always fixed and Burns and several of the racers he looked up to are nothing but corporate shills whose "wins" were always planned.Speed:Mr. Burns? The '43 Prix. Did...you know you were going to win?Ben Burns:Y'know, everybody thought that me and Stickleton hated each other. Funny, ain't it? Fake Ultimate Hero: A racing icon and one of Speed's personal heroes whose defining victory turned out to have been orchestrated by greedy corporations the entire time. Forced into Evil: Implied at the end.The fact that he's celebrating Speed's victory at the end, which also exposed the public to race fixing and Royalton's crimes, indicates that he wasn't happy participating in rigged races.
